name: What structural considerations are required when switching to a curbless walk-in shower?

mainEntity.name: What structural considerations are required when switching to a curbless walk-in shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: A curbless walk-in shower requires lowering the subfloor or installing a specialized recessed drain pan so the bathroom floor meets the shower entrance without a step. This requires checking joist direction, structural framing depth, and door clearance before demolition begins. Curbless designs significantly improve accessibility and deliver a sleek, modern look, but they demand precise floor slope angles and wider splash zones to keep water from escaping. By contrast, a standard curbed shower retains water easily in smaller footprints and involves less structural subfloor alteration.
acceptedAnswer.description: Curbless showers require lowering the subfloor framing or using recessed pan systems to create an unobstructed entry while maintaining adequate slope for drainage.
